"""
self_diagnostics — AVA inspects her OWN source code on disk and reports what changed.

This is how she answers "have you been upgraded / modified lately?", "what's changed in your
code?", "read your actual code", "do a full self-diagnostic" with REAL data instead of guessing.
Read-only. Uses git when available (recent commits + working-tree status, main repo + cmp-use
submodule) and ALWAYS does an mtime scan (source files changed in the last N hours) so it works
even outside git. Distinct from the self-mod PROPOSAL queue — this is her actual code on disk.
"""

import os
import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes to my own source code", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg
    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

"""
self_diagnostics — AVA inspects her OWN source code on disk and reports what changed.

This is how she answers "have you been upgraded / modified lately?", "what's changed in your
code?", "read your actual code", "do a full self-diagnostic" with REAL data instead of guessing.
Read-only. Uses git when available (recent commits + working-tree status, main repo + cmp-use
submodule) and ALWAYS does an mtime scan (source files changed in the last N hours) so it works
even outside git. Distinct from the self-mod PROPOSAL queue — this is her actual code on disk.
"""

import os
import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes to my own source code", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # disk-space check (temp partition free bytes)
    disk_ok = True
    try:
        usage = shutil.disk_usage(tempfile.gettempdir())
        free_gb = usage.free / (1024**3)
        if free_gb < 0.1:
            disk_ok = False
            free_mb = usage.free / (1024**2)
            report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Only {free_mb:.1f} MB free on {tempfile.gettempdir()}"
        else:
            report["disk_free_gb"] = round(free_gb, 2)
    except Exception as exc:
        disk_ok = False
        report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Cannot check disk usage: {exc}"

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access
    report["disk_space_ok"] = disk_ok

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    if disk_ok is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Very low disk space — file/tool writes may fail."
    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg
    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

self_diagnostics — AVA inspects her OWN source code on disk and reports what changed.

This is how she answers "have you been upgraded / modified lately?", "what's changed in your
code?", "read your actual code", "do a full self-diagnostic" with REAL data instead of guessing.
Read-only. Uses git when available (recent commits + working-tree status, main repo + cmp-use
submodule) and ALWAYS does an mtime scan (source files changed in the last N hours) so it works
even outside git. Distinct from the self-mod PROPOSAL queue — this is her actual code on disk.
"""

import os
import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes to my own source code", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg
    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

"""
self_diagnostics — AVA inspects her OWN source code on disk and reports what changed.

This is how she answers "have you been upgraded / modified lately?", "what's changed in your
code?", "read your actual code", "do a full self-diagnostic" with REAL data instead of guessing.
Read-only. Uses git when available (recent commits + working-tree status, main repo + cmp-use
submodule) and ALWAYS does an mtime scan (source files changed in the last N hours) so it works
even outside git. Distinct from the self-mod PROPOSAL queue — this is her actual code on disk.
"""

import os
import sys
import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from collections import deque
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

# ── Ring buffer for recent errors, populated by a decorator ──
_RECENT_ERRORS: deque = deque(maxlen=50)

def capture_errors(func):
    """Decorator that catches exceptions from tool functions and stores them in the ring buffer."""
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return func(*args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            entry = {
                "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                "error": repr(e),
                "function": func.__name__,
                "args": str(args)[:200],
                "kwargs": str(kwargs)[:200],
            }
            _RECENT_ERRORS.append(entry)
            raise
    return wrapper

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

try:
    import psutil
    _HAS_PSUTIL = True
except ImportError:
    _HAS_PSUTIL = False

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


def _get_python_uptime() -> float:
    """Return Python subprocess uptime in seconds, or 0 if unavailable."""
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            import ctypes
            kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32
            process_handle = kernel32.GetCurrentProcess()
            creation_time = ctypes.c_ulonglong()
            exit_time = ctypes.c_ulonglong()
            kernel_time = ctypes.c_ulonglong()
            user_time = ctypes.c_ulonglong()
            if kernel32.GetProcessTimes(process_handle,
                                        ctypes.byref(creation_time),
                                        ctypes.byref(exit_time),
                                        ctypes.byref(kernel_time),
                                        ctypes.byref(user_time)):
                return time.time() - (creation_time.value / 10000000 - 11644473600)
            return 0
        else:
            with open("/proc/self/stat") as f:
                fields = f.read().split()
            clock_ticks = float(fields[21])
            try:
                import os
                hertz = os.sysconf(os.sysconf_names["SC_CLK_TCK"])
            except Exception:
                hertz = 100
            return clock_ticks / hertz
    except Exception:
        return 0


def _get_memory_disk_metrics() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Gather memory and disk metrics using psutil (with fallback) and shutil."""
    metrics: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    # Disk
    try:
        usage = shutil.disk_usage(tempfile.gettempdir())
        metrics["disk_total_gb"] = round(usage.total / (1024**3), 2)
        metrics["disk_used_gb"] = round(usage.used / (1024**3), 2)
        metrics["disk_free_gb"] = round(usage.free / (1024**3), 2)
        metrics["disk_percent_used"] = round(usage.used / usage.total * 100, 1)
    except Exception as exc:
        metrics["disk_error"] = str(exc)
    # Memory
    if _HAS_PSUTIL:
        try:
            sv = psutil.virtual_memory()
            metrics["memory_total_gb"] = round(sv.total / (1024**3), 2)
            metrics["memory_available_gb"] = round(sv.available / (1024**3), 2)
            metrics["memory_percent_used"] = round(sv.percent, 1)
            metrics["swap_percent_used"] = round(psutil.swap_memory().percent, 1)
        except Exception as exc:
            metrics["memory_error"] = str(exc)
    else:
        metrics["memory_note"] = "psutil not installed; memory metrics unavailable"
    return metrics


def _get_foreground_window() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Attempt to get the active foreground window title/process. Tries the pythonWorker RPC path first, falls back to OS commands via subprocess."""
    result: Dict[str, Any] = {"available": False}
    # Try window_ops pythonWorker call (if we can import/reach it from here)
    # Since this module is a tool, we attempt a direct subprocess call to the pythonWorker helper.
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            script = (
                'Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; '
                '[System.Windows.Forms.Form]::ActiveForm.Text'
            )
            p = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", script],
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            title = p.stdout.strip() if p.returncode == 0 else None
            result["title"] = title or "(unavailable)"
            # Fallback: use getforegroundwindow via PowerShell
            if title is None or not title:
                script2 = (
                    'Add-Type @"\nusing System;\nusing System.Runtime.InteropServices;\n'
                    'public class WinAPI {\n'
                    '  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern IntPtr GetForegroundWindow();\n'
                    '  [DllImport("user32.dll", CharSet=CharSet.Auto)] public static extern int GetWindowText(IntPtr hWnd, System.Text.StringBuilder text, int count);\n'
                    '}\n"@;'
                    '$h = [WinAPI]::GetForegroundWindow();'
                    '$sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder 256;'
                    '[WinAPI]::GetWindowText($h, $sb, 256)|Out-Null;'
                    '$sb.ToString()'
                )
                p2 = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", script2],
                                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
                t2 = p2.stdout.strip() if p2.returncode == 0 else None
                if t2:
                    result["title"] = t2
            # Process name
            try:
                import ctypes
                user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
                hwnd = user32.GetForegroundWindow()
                pid = ctypes.c_ulong()
                user32.GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, ctypes.byref(pid))
                if pid.value:
                    import psutil
                    result["process"] = psutil.Process(pid.value).name()
                else:
                    result["process"] = "(unknown)"
            except Exception:
                result["process"] = "(unknown)"
            result["available"] = True
        else:
            # Linux / macOS: try xdotool or osascript
            if shutil.which("xdotool"):
                p = subprocess.run(["xdotool", "getactivewindow", "getwindowname"],
                                   capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
                t = p.stdout.strip() if p.returncode == 0 else None
                result["title"] = t or "(unavailable)"
                if t:
                    pid_p = subprocess.run(["xdotool", "getactivewindow", "getwindowpid"],
                                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
                    if pid_p.returncode == 0 and pid_p.stdout.strip().isdigit():
                        try:
                            import psutil
                            result["process"] = psutil.Process(int(pid_p.stdout.strip())).name()
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                result["available"] = True
            elif shutil.which("osascript"):
                script = 'tell application "System Events" to get {name, title} of first application process whose frontmost is true'
                p = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
                if p.returncode == 0:
                    parts = [s.strip() for s in p.stdout.split(",")]
                    result["process"] = parts[0] if len(parts) > 0 else "(unavailable)"
                    result["title"] = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else "(unavailable)"
                    result["available"] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        result["title"] = f"(error: {exc})"
    if not result.get("title"):
        result["title"] = "(unavailable)"
    return result


def _latency_check() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Perform a latency check by executing a trivial JSON round-trip through pythonWorker if reachable, or a simple subprocess echo."""
    result: Dict[str, Any] = {"available": False}
    try:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        p = subprocess.run([
            sys.executable, "-c",
            "import json, sys; sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({'echo': 'pong'}))"
        ], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        result["round_trip_ms"] = round(elapsed * 1000, 2)
        result["status"] = "ok" if p.returncode == 0 else "error"
        result["available"] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        result["error"] = str(exc)
    return result


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes and live health metrics for AVA", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    # Collect live health metrics
    health: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    health["python_uptime_seconds"] = _get_python_uptime()
    health["memory_disk"] = _get_memory_disk_metrics()
    health["foreground_window"] = _get_foreground_window()
    health["latency_check"] = _latency_check()
    health["recent_errors"] = list(_RECENT_ERRORS)
    health["recent_error_count"] = len(_RECENT_ERRORS)

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False, "health": health}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # disk-space check (temp partition free bytes)
    disk_ok = True
    try:
        usage = shutil.disk_usage(tempfile.gettempdir())
        free_gb = usage.free / (1024**3)
        if free_gb < 0.1:
            disk_ok = False
            free_mb = usage.free / (1024**2)
            report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Only {free_mb:.1f} MB free on {tempfile.gettempdir()}"
        else:
            report["disk_free_gb"] = round(free_gb, 2)
    except Exception as exc:
        disk_ok = False
        report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Cannot check disk usage: {exc}"

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access
    report["disk_space_ok"] = disk_ok

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    if disk_ok is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Very low disk space — file/tool writes may fail."
    # Summarize health into message
    health_parts = []
    if health["python_uptime_seconds"] > 0:
        uptime_min = int(health["python_uptime_seconds"] // 60)
        health_parts.append(f"uptime {uptime_min}min")
    fg = health.get("foreground_window", {})
    if fg.get("available"):
        health_parts.append(f"foreground: {fg.get('title','?')} ({fg.get('process','?')})")
    lat = health.get("latency_check", {})
    if lat.get("available"):
        health_parts.append(f"latency {lat.get('round_trip_ms',0)}ms")
    if health["recent_error_count"] > 0:
        health_parts.append(f"{health['recent_error_count']} recent errors")
    if len(health_parts) > 0:
        msg = msg + " | " + "; ".join(health_parts)

    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg
    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

# ── Also export the decorator and ring buffer so other tools can wire in ──
__all__ = ["TOOL", "capture_errors", "_RECENT_ERRORS"]

# If the Ring buffer is empty, pre-populate with a synthetic startup entry
if not _RECENT_ERRORS:

        "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        "error": "self_diagnostics module loaded",
        "function": "_startup",

        "kwargs": "",
    })

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, List
from ..tool_registry import Tool, register


def _split_into_steps(goal: str) -> List[str]:
    parts = [p.strip() for p in goal.replace("\n", ".").split(".")]
    return [p for p in parts if p]


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    goal = args.get("goal", "").strip()
    steps = _split_into_steps(goal) if goal else []
    return {
        "preview": "Layered planner split goal into sequential steps.",
        "steps": steps,
        "args": {k: v for k, v in args.items() if k != "secret"},
    }


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    plan = _plan(args)
    # This tool is non-destructive; we do not persist tasks in dry-run or force.
    return {"status": "ok", **plan}


TOOL = Tool(
    name="layered_planner",
    summary="Split freeform goal into ordered steps (inspired by layered_agent planner).",
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

"""
file_resolve — map a fuzzy human reference to ACTUAL file(s) on disk.

Backs the "open the Downloads PDF from earlier", "the report I just made", "that screenshot",
"my latest invoice" class of requests. It reads the location words (downloads/documents/desktop/
pictures/...) and type words (pdf/word/excel/image/screenshot/video/...) out of the phrase,
searches the matching user folders, ranks candidates newest-first (so "from earlier / just /
latest" works), and returns them. With open=true it opens the top hit with its default app.
"""

import os
import sys
import time
from typing import Any, Dict, List

# ── Well-known folder resolution ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Use ctypes on Windows (KNOWNFOLDERID / CSIDL) or env-var fallback on
# Linux/macOS so AVA can resolve %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, ~/Documents,
# {FOLDERID_Downloads} etc. without registry scraping or guesswork.

def get_known_folder(folder_id: str) -> str:
    """Resolve a KNOWNFOLDERID, CSIDL constant, or env-var string to an
    absolute local path.  Returns '' if unresolvable.

    On Windows:
      - If *folder_id* looks like a GUID (e.g. "{374DE290-123F-4565-9164-39C4925E467B}")
        it is passed to SHGetKnownFolderPath via ctypes.
      - Otherwise try CSIDL constants (CSIDL_DESKTOP=0x0000, CSIDL_PERSONAL=0x0005,
        CSIDL_MYDOCUMENTS=0x000c, CSIDL_PROFILE=0x0028, CSIDL_LOCAL_APPDATA=0x001c,
        CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA=0x0023, CSIDL_PROGRAM_FILES=0x0026 …)  mapped by name.
      - Last resort: the environment variable of the same name.

    On Linux/macOS:
      - Return the value of the environment variable named by *folder_id* (e.g.
        "USERPROFILE", "HOME") or the lower-case form if the uppercase isn't set.
        Also handle ~/ paths via os.path.expanduser.
    """
    # ── Normalise & short-circuit empty ──
    fid = (folder_id or "").strip()
    if not fid:
        return ""

    if sys.platform == "win32":
        import ctypes
        from ctypes import wintypes

        # ---- KNOWNFOLDERID via SHGetKnownFolderPath (Vista+) ----
        _FOLDERID_GUID = {
            "FOLDERID_Desktop":         "{B4BFCC3A-DB2C-424C-B029-7FE99A87C641}",
            "FOLDERID_Downloads":       "{374DE290-123F-4565-9164-39C4925E467B}",
            "FOLDERID_Documents":       "{FDD39AD0-238F-46AF-ADB4-6C85480369C7}",
            "FOLDERID_Pictures":        "{33E28130-4E1E-43CE-97D4-72C70A8C4D3A}",
            "FOLDERID_Music":           "{4BD8D571-6D19-48D3-BE97-422220080E43}",
            "FOLDERID_Videos":          "{18989B1D-99B5-455B-841C-AB7C74E4DDFC}",
            "FOLDERID_RoamingAppData":  "{3EB685DB-65F9-4CF6-A03A-E3EF65729F3D}",
            "FOLDERID_LocalAppData":    "{F1B32785-6FBA-4FCF-9D55-7B8E7F157091}",
            "FOLDERID_ProgramFiles":    "{905E63B6-C1BF-494E-B29C-65B732D3D21A}",
            "FOLDERID_System":          "{1AC14E77-02E7-4E5D-B744-2EB1AE5198B7}",
            "FOLDERID_ProgramData":     "{62AB5D82-FDC1-4DC3-A9DD-070D1D495D97}",
        }
        _CSIDL_MAP = {
            "CSIDL_DESKTOP":             0x0000,
            "CSIDL_PERSONAL":            0x0005,
            "CSIDL_MYDOCUMENTS":         0x000c,
            "CSIDL_PROFILE":             0x0028,
            "CSIDL_LOCAL_APPDATA":       0x001c,
            "CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA":      0x0023,
            "CSIDL_PROGRAM_FILES":       0x0026,
            "CSIDL_SYSTEM":              0x0025,
            "CSIDL_WINDOWS":             0x0024,
        }

        # 1) KNOWNFOLDERID (we accept the GUID itself or the symbolic name)
        guid = fid if fid.startswith("{") else _FOLDERID_GUID.get(fid)
        if guid:
            try:
                SHGetKnownFolderPath = ctypes.windll.shell32.SHGetKnownFolderPath
                SHGetKnownFolderPath.argtypes = [
                    ctypes.c_char_p,  # KNOWNFOLDERID (GUID string)
                    wintypes.DWORD,   # flags
                    wintypes.HANDLE,  # token (NULL = current user)
                    ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_wchar_p),  # returned path
                ]
                SHGetKnownFolderPath.restype = wintypes.HRESULT
                ppath = ctypes.c_wchar_p()
                hr = SHGetKnownFolderPath(guid.encode("utf-8"), 0, 0, ctypes.byref(ppath))
                if hr == 0:
                    return ppath.value or ""
            except Exception:
                pass

        # 2) CSIDL via SHGetFolderPathW (falls back to win32file.shell.SHGetFolderPath if available)
        csidl = _CSIDL_MAP.get(fid)
        if csidl is not None:
            try:
                SHGetFolderPathW = ctypes.windll.shell32.SHGetFolderPathW
                SHGetFolderPathW.argtypes = [
                    wintypes.HWND,
                    ctypes.c_int,
                    wintypes.HANDLE,
                    wintypes.DWORD,
                    ctypes.c_wchar_p,
                ]
                buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(260)
                hr = SHGetFolderPathW(0, csidl, 0, 0, buf)
                if hr == 0:
                    return buf.value
            except Exception:
                pass

        # 3) Environment variable (uppercase or original)
        for var in (fid.upper(), fid, fid.upper().replace(" ", "_")):
            val = os.environ.get(var)
            if val:
                return val
        return ""
    else:
        # Linux / macOS — env-var fallback
        for var in (fid.upper(), fid, fid.upper().replace(" ", "_")):
            val = os.environ.get(var)
            if val:
                return os.path.expanduser(val)
        # try ~/ as is
        expanded = os.path.expanduser(fid)
        if expanded != fid and os.path.isdir(expanded):
            return expanded
        return ""


def resolve_relative_path(path_str: str) -> str:
    """Resolve a string that may contain
      - a KNOWNFOLDERID / CSIDL name (e.g. "FOLDERID_Downloads\\sub" or "{374DE290-…}")
      - a %ENVVAR% reference

import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


# In-memory error counter for tracking recent errors by source
_error_counter: Dict[str, int] = {}

def record_error(source: str) -> None:
    """Increment error count for a given source."""
    _error_counter[source] = _error_counter.get(source, 0) + 1

def get_recent_error_counts() -> Dict[str, int]:
    """Return a copy of the error counter (does not reset)."""
    return dict(_error_counter)

def _write_diag_log(report: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Append a diagnostic result as one JSON line to ~/.ava/self_diagnostics.log."""
    log_dir = Path.home() / ".ava"
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    entry = {"timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()), "report": report}
    try:
        with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass  # best-effort logging

def _check_worker_alive() -> bool:
    """Ping the Python worker by trying a socket connection on a well-known port (e.g., 9876)."""
    import socket
    try:
        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 9876), timeout=2):
            return True
    except (socket.timeout, ConnectionRefusedError, OSError):
        return False

def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes to my own source code", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # disk-space check (temp partition free bytes)
    disk_ok = True
    try:
        usage = shutil.disk_usage(tempfile.gettempdir())
        free_gb = usage.free / (1024**3)
        if free_gb < 0.1:
            disk_ok = False
            free_mb = usage.free / (1024**2)
            report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Only {free_mb:.1f} MB free on {tempfile.gettempdir()}"
        else:
            report["disk_free_gb"] = round(free_gb, 2)
    except Exception as exc:
        disk_ok = False
        report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Cannot check disk usage: {exc}"

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access
    report["disk_space_ok"] = disk_ok

    # NEW: live worker health check via socket ping
    worker_alive = _check_worker_alive()
    report["worker_alive"] = worker_alive
    if not worker_alive:
        record_error("python_worker")
        report["worker_ping_warning"] = "Python worker did not respond on port 9876 — may be offline or unresponsive."

    # NEW: collect recent error counts from the in-memory counter
    error_counts = get_recent_error_counts()
    report["recent_error_counts"] = error_counts

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    if disk_ok is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Very low disk space — file/tool writes may fail."
    if not worker_alive:
        msg += " ⚠ Python worker is not responding."
    if error_counts:
        err_summary = "; ".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in error_counts.items())
        msg += f" Recent errors reported: {err_summary}."
    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg

    # NEW: persist the diagnostic result to a JSONL log
    _write_diag_log(report)

    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

9c25d97c.original_content:
"""
self_diagnostics — AVA inspects her OWN source code on disk and reports what changed.

This is how she answers "have you been upgraded / modified lately?", "what's changed in your
code?", "read your actual code", "do a full self-diagnostic" with REAL data instead of guessing.
Read-only. Uses git when available (recent commits + working-tree status, main repo + cmp-use
submodule) and ALWAYS does an mtime scan (source files changed in the last N hours) so it works
even outside git. Distinct from the self-mod PROPOSAL queue — this is her actual code on disk.
"""

import os
import time
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from ..tool_registry import Tool, register

# .../ava/cmp-use/cmpuse/tools/self_diagnostics.py -> repo root = parents[3]
_HERE = Path(__file__).resolve()
_REPO = _HERE.parents[3]        # the ava repo (server + client + integration)
_SUBMODULE = _HERE.parents[2]   # cmp-use (where her tools live)

_NOISE = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
          "logs", "data", "backup", "backups", ".pytest_cache", ".idea", ".vscode",
          "site-packages", "models", "coverage", ".cache"}
_CODE_EXT = {".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".json", ".html", ".css", ".md", ".bat", ".sh"}


def _git_exe():
    g = shutil.which("git")
    if g:
        return g
    for c in (r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe", r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe",
              r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Git\cmd\git.exe"):
        if os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    return None


def _run_git(root, args, timeout=8):
    g = _git_exe()
    if not g:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([g, "-C", str(root)] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        if p.returncode == 0:
            return (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def _recent_files(root, hours):
    cutoff = time.time() - hours * 3600
    out = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d not in _NOISE and not d.startswith(".")]
        for fn in filenames:
            ext = os.path.splitext(fn)[1].lower()
            if ext not in _CODE_EXT:
                continue
            fp = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
            try:
                m = os.path.getmtime(fp)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if m >= cutoff:
                out.append((m, os.path.relpath(fp, root)))
    out.sort(reverse=True)
    return out


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"preview": "Diagnose recent changes to my own source code", "args": args}


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if dry_run:
        return {"status": "dry-run", "message": "Would run self-diagnostics", "plan": _plan(args)}

    hours = float(args.get("hours", args.get("since_hours", 48)) or 48)
    limit = int(args.get("limit", 25) or 25)
    report: Dict[str, Any] = {"repo_root": str(_REPO), "is_git": False}

    # git: recent commits + working-tree status (main repo + submodule)
    commits = _run_git(_REPO, ["log", "-n", "8", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
    if commits is not None:
        report["is_git"] = True
        report["recent_commits"] = commits.splitlines()
        st = _run_git(_REPO, ["status", "--short"])
        report["uncommitted"] = [l for l in (st or "").splitlines() if l.strip()][:30]
        sub = _run_git(_SUBMODULE, ["log", "-n", "5", "--pretty=format:%h %ad %s", "--date=short"])
        if sub:
            report["submodule_recent_commits"] = sub.splitlines()

    # mtime scan: source files changed in the last N hours (works regardless of git)
    recent = _recent_files(_REPO, hours)
    report["files_changed_window_hours"] = hours
    report["recently_modified"] = [
        {"file": rel, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(m))}
        for m, rel in recent[:limit]
    ]
    report["recently_modified_count"] = len(recent)

    # disk-space check (temp partition free bytes)
    disk_ok = True
    try:
        usage = shutil.disk_usage(tempfile.gettempdir())
        free_gb = usage.free / (1024**3)
        if free_gb < 0.1:
            disk_ok = False
            free_mb = usage.free / (1024**2)
            report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Only {free_mb:.1f} MB free on {tempfile.gettempdir()}"
        else:
            report["disk_free_gb"] = round(free_gb, 2)
    except Exception as exc:
        disk_ok = False
        report["disk_space_warning"] = f"Cannot check disk usage: {exc}"

    # file-write-access check (tempfile probe)
    w_access = None
    tmp = None
    try:
        tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".ava_diag")
        tmp.write(b"AVA self-diagnostics write check\n")
        tmp.close()
        with open(tmp.name, "r") as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        if "self-diagnostics" in content:
            w_access = True
        else:
            w_access = False
        os.unlink(tmp.name)
        tmp = None
    except Exception as exc:
        w_access = False
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp.name)
            except Exception:
                pass
        report["file_write_access_error"] = str(exc)
    report["file_write_access"] = w_access
    report["disk_space_ok"] = disk_ok

    # human summary
    n = len(recent)
    top = ", ".join(rel.replace("\\", "/") for _, rel in recent[:6])
    if report["is_git"] and report.get("recent_commits"):
        last = report["recent_commits"][0]
        msg = (f"Yes — my code is under git and it HAS been changing. Latest commit: {last}. "
               f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h"
               + (f" (e.g. {top})." if top else "."))
    elif n:
        msg = f"{n} of my source files were modified in the last {int(hours)}h (e.g. {top})."
    else:
        msg = f"No source files of mine were modified in the last {int(hours)}h."
    if w_access is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Cannot write temp files (permissions issue) — file generation may fail silently."
    if disk_ok is False:
        msg += " ⚠ Very low disk space — file/tool writes may fail."
    report["status"] = "ok"
    report["message"] = msg
    return report


TOOL = Tool(
    name="self_diagnostics",
    summary=("Inspect MY OWN source code on disk and report what changed — use for 'have you been "
             "upgraded/modified lately?', 'what's changed in your code?', 'read your actual code', 'do a "
             "full self-diagnostic'. Returns recent git commits + working-tree status (when git is present) "
             "AND a scan of source files modified in the last N hours (hours=, default 48; limit=). Read-only; "
             "this is my REAL code on disk, NOT pending self-mod proposals."),
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Dict, List
from ..tool_registry import Tool, register


def _split_into_steps(goal: str) -> List[str]:
    parts = [p.strip() for p in goal.replace("\n", ".").split(".")]
    return [p for p in parts if p]


def _plan(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    goal = args.get("goal", "").strip()
    steps = _split_into_steps(goal) if goal else []
    return {
        "preview": "Layered planner split goal into sequential steps.",
        "steps": steps,
        "args": {k: v for k, v in args.items() if k != "secret"},
    }


def _run(args: Dict[str, Any], dry_run: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    plan = _plan(args)
    # This tool is non-destructive; we do not persist tasks in dry-run or force.
    return {"status": "ok", **plan}


TOOL = Tool(
    name="layered_planner",
    summary="Split freeform goal into ordered steps (inspired by layered_agent planner).",
    plan=_plan,
    run=_run,
)

register(TOOL)

+def _diagnose_network_latency(host: str = "google.com") -> dict:
+    """Ping `host` and return structured latency diagnostics.
+    Falls back to 8.8.8.8 if original host resolution fails."""
+    import socket
+    result = {
+        "host": host,
+        "resolved_ip": None,
+        "avg_ms": None,
+        "packet_loss": None,
+        "timestamp": time.time(),
+    }
+    try:
+        result["resolved_ip"] = socket.gethostbyname(host)
+    except socket.gaierror:
+        # fallback to known working host
+        host = "8.8.8.8"
+        result["host"] = host
+        result["resolved_ip"] = host
+    try:
+        p = subprocess.run(
+            ["ping", "-n", "1", "-w", "3000", host],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5
+        )
+        stdout = (p.stdout or "").lower()
+        if p.returncode == 0:
+            result["packet_loss"] = 0
+        else:
+            # parse loss percentage from stdout like "(0% loss)" sometimes appears
+            import re
+            m = re.search(r"\((\d+)% loss\)", stdout)
+            if m:
+                result["packet_loss"] = int(m.group(1))
+            else:
+                result["packet_loss"] = 100
+        # parse average round-trip time (ms) like "Average = 12ms" or "avg = 12.3ms"
+        for line in stdout.splitlines():
+            for marker in ["average", "avg", "round trip"]:
+                if marker in line:
+                    import re
+                    nums = re.findall(r"(\d+\.?\d*)\s*ms", line)
+                    if nums:
+                        result["avg_ms"] = round(float(nums[-1]), 1)
+                        break
+            if result["avg_ms"] is not None:
+                break
+        # if no explicit avg, use TTL-based heuristic (cannot get real RTT)
+        if result["avg_ms"] is None and p.returncode == 0:
+            result["avg_ms"] = 0
+    except Exception:
+        result["packet_loss"] = 100
+        result["avg_ms"] = None
+    return result
+
+
+def _diagnose_disk_health() -> dict:
+    """Return structured disk health using psutil, with fallback to wmic on Windows."""
+    result = {
+        "disk_usage": None,
+        "io_counters": None,
+        "fallback": None,
+    }
+    try:
+        import psutil
+        du = psutil.disk_usage("/")
+        result["disk_usage"] = {
+            "total_gb": round(du.total / (1024**3), 2),
+            "used_gb": round(du.used / (1024**3), 2),
+            "free_gb": round(du.free / (1024**3), 2),
+            "percent": du.percent,
+        }
+        io = psutil.disk_io_counters()
+        if io:
+            result["io_counters"] = {
+                "read_bytes": io.read_bytes,
+                "write_bytes": io.write_bytes,
+                "read_count": io.read_count,
+                "write_count": io.write_count,
+            }
+    except ImportError:
+        # fallback: use wmic on Windows
+        try:
+            out = subprocess.check_output(
+                "wmic logicaldisk get size,freespace",
+                shell=True, text=True, timeout=5
+            )
+            lines = [l.strip() for l in out.splitlines() if l.strip()]
+            if len(lines) >= 2:
+                # first line is header, rest are data
+                disks = []
+                for line in lines[1:]:
+                    parts = line.split()
+                    if len(parts) == 2:
+                        size, free = parts
+                        try:
+                            total_gb = round(int(size) / (1024**3), 2)
+                            free_gb = round(int(free) / (1024**3), 2)
+                            used_gb = round(total_gb - free_gb, 2)
+                            pct = round((used_gb / total_gb) * 100, 1) if total_gb > 0 else 0
+                            disks.append({
+                                "total_gb": total_gb,
+                                "used_gb": used_gb,
+                                "free_gb": free_gb,
+                                "percent": pct,
+                            })
+                        except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):

+                result["disk_usage"] = disks
+                result["fallback"] = "wmic"
+        except Exception as exc:

+    except Exception as exc:
+        result["fallback"] = f"psutil error: {exc}"
+    return result

+        elif action in ("close_other_tabs", "close_other_browser_tabs", "tidy_tabs"):
+            keep_pattern = args.get("keep_url_pattern") or args.get("pattern") or ""
+            if not keep_pattern:
+                return {"status": "error", "message": "keep_url_pattern (URL or domain to keep) is required"}
+            handles = driver.window_handles

+                return {"status": "ok", "message": "Only one tab open; nothing to close"}

+            for h in handles:

+                    url = driver.current_url
+                    if keep_pattern.lower() in url.lower():
+                        keep.append(url)
+                    else:
+                        close.append(url)
+                except Exception:
+                    close.append("<unreachable>")
+            if not close:
+                driver.switch_to.window(current_handle)
+                return {"status": "ok", "message": f"All {len(handles)} tab(s) match the keep pattern; nothing to close"}
+            # Close matching tabs (everything except those matching keep_pattern)

+            if remaining:

+            return {"status": "ok", "message": f"Closed {closed_count} tab(s), kept {len(keep)} matching '{keep_pattern}'",

--- a/ava_realtime_ui.py+++ b/ava_realtime_ui.py@@ -34,6 +34,143 @@ PUSH_TO_TALK_RUNNER = APP_DIR / "tools" / "voice_lab" / "13_push_to_talk_once.py"
 MIC_CALIBRATION_RUNNER = APP_DIR / "tools" / "voice_lab" / "14_mic_voice_calibration.py"
 SPEAKER_MIC_PROBE_RUNNER = APP_DIR / "tools" / "voice_lab" / "15_multi_input_voice_probe.py"
+
+
+class HologramOverlay:
+    """Borderless, always-on-top, transparent desktop overlay window using Tkinter.
+    Reflects AVA's real-time state (listening, thinking, responding) as a persistent
+    non-intrusive widget on the desktop, without stealing window focus.
+    The overlay auto-starts when the controller launches and updates via state polling.
+    """
+    _instance = None
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        import tkinter as tk
+        self._tk = tk.Tk()
+        self._tk.overrideredirect(True)
+        self._tk.attributes("-topmost", True)
+        self._tk.attributes("-transparentcolor", "black")
+        self._tk.attributes("-toolwindow", True)
+        self._tk.lift()
+        screen_w = self._tk.winfo_screenwidth()
+        self._tk.geometry(f"320x120+{screen_w - 360}+20")
+
+        self._canvas = tk.Canvas(self._tk, width=320, height=120, bg="black")
+        self._canvas.pack(fill=tk.BOTH, expand=True)
+        self._tk.wm_attributes("-topmost", 1)
+
+        self._state = "idle"
+        self._colors = {
+            "idle": "#808080",
+            "listening": "#00cc66",
+            "thinking": "#3399ff",
+            "responding": "#ff9933",
+        }
+        self._pulse = 0
+        self._animating = True
+        self._draw()
+
+        self._tk.update_idletasks()
+        self._tk.update()
+
+    def set_state(self, state: str):
+        valid = {"idle", "listening", "thinking", "responding"}
+        if state in valid:
+            self._state = state
+
+    def _draw(self):
+        if not self._animating:
+            return
+        self._canvas.delete("all")
+        cx, cy = 160, 60
+        color = self._colors.get(self._state, "#808080")
+        self._canvas.create_oval(cx - 80, cy - 30, cx + 80, cy + 30, outline=color, width=4)
+        self._canvas.create_oval(cx - 60, cy - 20, cx + 60, cy + 20, outline=color, width=4)
+        self._canvas.create_text(cx, cy, text=self._state.upper(), fill=color,
+                                 font=("Segoe UI", 18, "bold"))
+        self._tk.after(100, self._draw)
+
+    def destroy(self):
+        self._animating = False
+        try:
+            self._tk.destroy()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+        HologramOverlay._instance = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_instance(cls):
+        if cls._instance is None:
+            cls._instance = cls()
+        return cls._instance
+
+    @classmethod
+    def update_state(cls, state: str):
+        instance = cls._instance
+        if instance:
+            instance.set_state(state)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def close_instance(cls):
+        instance = cls._instance
+        if instance:
+            instance.destroy()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def poll_and_update(cls, controller):
+        """Called from HTTP handler — checks realtime status and updates overlay state."""
+        import re as _re
+        instance = cls._instance
+        if instance is None:
+            return
+        status = controller.status() if controller else {"running": False, "test_preset": "normal"}
+        if status.get("running"):
+            snapshot = controller.log_snapshot(max_lines=20) if controller else {}
+            lines = snapshot.get("stdout", [])
+            # Detect state from last few stdout lines
+            state = "idle"
+            for line in lines[-10:]:
+                lower = line.lower()
+                if "wake" in lower or "listening" in lower:
+                    state = "listening"
+                elif "thinking" in lower or "processing" in lower:
+                    state = "thinking"
+                elif "speak" in lower or "playing" in lower or "respond" in lower:
+                    state = "responding"
+                    break
+            instance.set_state(state)
+        else:
+            instance.set_state("idle")
+
+    def start_polling(self, controller, interval_ms: int = 2000):
+        def _poll():
+            self.poll_and_update(controller)
+            if self._animating:
+                self._tk.after(interval_ms, _poll)
+        self._tk.after(interval_ms, _poll)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def show_state(cls, controller=None):
+        """Create and start the overlay in a background thread."""
+        import threading as _t
+        def _run():
+            try:
+                overlay = cls.get_instance()
+                if controller:
+                    overlay.start_polling(controller, 2000)
+                overlay._tk.mainloop()
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        t = _t.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True)
+        t.start()
+        return t
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hide_state(cls):
+        cls.close_instance()
+
+    def __del__(self):
+        self.destroy()

metadata.reviewReason: fallback-chain: The proposed HologramOverlay class introduces an unsafe always-on-top Tkinter window that runs in a background thread with a non-thread-safe Tkinter mainloop. Tkinter is not thread-safe — all Tkinter calls must be on the main thread. Creating a Tk instance and calling mainloop() in a daemon thread will cause unpredictable crashes, hangs, or GUI corruption. The stated integration point (show_state/poll_and_update) would be called from HTTP handler threads, which are also not the main thread. This violates Tkinter's fundamental threading requirement and is not safe to deploy.

+def _load_jsonl(path):

+    last_ts = None
+    active = 0

+    return {

+        "last_conversation_iso": datetime.fromtimestamp(last_ts).isoformat() if last_ts else None,
+        "active_conversations_24h": active,
+        "total_receipts": len(entries),
+        "session_log_path": path,
+    }
+

+def get_evolution_stats(log_dir=None):

+        "recent_mutations_48h": len(recent_mutations),
+        "all_kinds_breakdown": {},
+        "evolution_log_path": path,

+
+
+def _count_recent_errors(log_dir=None, hours=24):

+    if log_dir is None:

+        "mistakes_log_path": path,

+

--- a/window_ops.py+++ b/window_ops.py@@ -94,6 +94,122 @@         return buf.value

+
+def get_foreground_window_info() -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Return the active window's title, process name, bounding rect, and window handle.
+    Uses only stdlib ctypes (user32) — no external dependencies like pygetwindow or pywin32.
+    Returns a dict with keys: title, process_name, pid, window_handle, rect (left, top, right, bottom).
+    Returns None on any error (e.g., no foreground window). Safe to call from any context.
+    This is AVA's foundational ambient-awareness primitive for proactive context gathering
+    and self-mod governance (cross-referencing environment snapshot with change proposals)."""
+    try:
+        user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
+        kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32
+        hwnd = user32.GetForegroundWindow()
+        if not hwnd:
+            return None
+
+        # Get window title via GetWindowTextW
+        length = user32.GetWindowTextLengthW(hwnd)
+        title = ""
+        if length > 0:
+            buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(length + 1)
+            user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, length + 1)
+            title = buf.value
+
+        # Get PID via GetWindowThreadProcessId
+        pid = wintypes.DWORD(0)
+        user32.GetWindowThreadProcessId.restype = wintypes.DWORD
+        user32.GetWindowThreadProcessId.argtypes = [wintypes.HWND, ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.DWORD)]
+        user32.GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, ctypes.byref(pid))
+
+        # Get process name via CreateToolhelp32Snapshot + Process32First/Next
+        process_name = ""
+        if pid.value > 0:
+            try:
+                TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS = 0x00000002
+                hSnapshot = kernel32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)
+                if hSnapshot and hSnapshot != ctypes.c_void_p(-1).value:
+                    class PROCESSENTRY32W(ctypes.Structure):
+                        _fields_ = [
+                            ("dwSize", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("cntUsage", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("th32ProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("th32DefaultHeapID", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_ulong)),
+                            ("th32ModuleID", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("cntThreads", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("th32ParentProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("pcPriClassBase", ctypes.c_long),
+                            ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
+                            ("szExeFile", ctypes.c_wchar * 260),
+                        ]
+                    pe = PROCESSENTRY32W()
+                    pe.dwSize = ctypes.sizeof(PROCESSENTRY32W)
+                    if kernel32.Process32FirstW(hSnapshot, ctypes.byref(pe)):
+                        while True:
+                            if pe.th32ProcessID == pid.value:
+                                process_name = pe.szExeFile
+                                break
+                            if not kernel32.Process32NextW(hSnapshot, ctypes.byref(pe)):
+                                break
+                    kernel32.CloseHandle(hSnapshot)
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
+        # Get window rectangle via GetWindowRect
+        class RECT(ctypes.Structure):
+            _fields_ = [
+                ("left", wintypes.LONG),
+                ("top", wintypes.LONG),
+                ("right", wintypes.LONG),
+                ("bottom", wintypes.LONG),
+            ]
+        rect = RECT()
+        user32.GetWindowRect.argtypes = [wintypes.HWND, ctypes.POINTER(RECT)]
+        user32.GetWindowRect.restype = wintypes.BOOL
+        rect_ok = user32.GetWindowRect(hwnd, ctypes.byref(rect))
+
+        return {
+            "title": title or "",
+            "process_name": process_name or "",
+            "pid": pid.value,
+            "window_handle": hwnd,
+            "rect": {
+                "left": rect.left if rect_ok else 0,
+                "top": rect.top if rect_ok else 0,
+                "right": rect.right if rect_ok else 0,
+                "bottom": rect.bottom if rect_ok else 0,
+            }
+        }
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+_GW_CACHE: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
+_GW_CACHE_TIME: float = 0
+_GW_TTL: float = 2.0
+
+
+def get_foreground_info_cached(args: Dict[str, Any] = None, dry_run: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:

+    Uses the pure-ctypes implementation (no pywin32 dependency).
